events.title: Frühlingswind
events.text: Combat Command A of the US 1st Armored Division, under Brig. Gen. Raymond McQuillin, holds the plain round Sidi Bou Zid below the Eastern Dorsal: Lt. Col. John Waters's force on Djebel Lessouda to the north, the 3rd Battalion, 168th Infantry on Djebel Ksaïra to the south-east, Hightower's tank battalion in reserve by the village, and the guns by the village and along the road to Aïn Rebaou. Operation Frühlingswind sends two panzer divisions under General Heinz Ziegler against it: the 10th through Faïd Pass, the 21st round the south by Maizila Pass. At four in the morning, in a sandstorm, Maj. Hudel's tank battalion moves off from the olive grove east of Faïd.

events.title: Out of Faïd Pass
events.text: German guns have shelled the Lessouda road junction since six. At 6:30 the Germans come out of Faïd Pass onto a misty plain, the light 'not yet sufficient'. Kampfgruppe Gerhardt swings round the north of Djebel Lessouda; Kampfgruppe Reimann, with a company of Tigers, comes down the Faïd–Sbeïtla road. Company G, 1st Armored Regiment, ten tanks east of Lessouda, is hit at once and Maj. Norman Parsons's tank knocked out. Col. Peter Hains in Sidi Bou Zid hears the gunfire at '06:35 hours, by my watch'.

events.title: Hightower goes forward
events.text: About 7:30 Lt. Col. Louis Hightower is ordered to 'clear up the situation' with two tank companies of the 3rd Battalion, 1st Armored Regiment and the tank destroyers of Company A, 701st. Howe gives the battalion about forty tanks. The 2nd Battalion, 168th Infantry on Lessouda reports itself surrounded from this hour.

events.title: The guns are shelled
events.text: At eight German guns shell the 17th Field Artillery heavily. Its 155 mm howitzers stand astride the Sidi Bou Zid–Aïn Rebaou road at the foot of Djebel Ksaïra. Col. Thomas Drake of the 168th Infantry sees 'the armored artillery followed by the 17th Field Artillery' leave their positions, telephones McQuillin, is told to 'take command and stop it', and stops it. Howe names the battalion as the 2nd; the 1st Armored Division's own report says the 1st. It was probably the 2nd. Where its batteries stood is not recorded: the map spaces three along the road by guesswork.

events.title: Lessouda cut off
events.text: By 8:30 more than forty German tanks have encircled Djebel Lessouda and are on the Faïd–Sbeïtla road heading south; at nine 39 Mark IVs and some Tigers are reported west of the hill. About 900 men of Waters's force are cut off on it.

events.title: Dive bombers
events.text: Between ten and eleven dive bombers and fighter-bombers hit the Sidi Bou Zid area. In the last hour of the morning Hightower pulls his tanks back south-west. About eleven McQuillin's line to Drake is cut after 'No more over the phone, we are leaving', and the CCA headquarters starts for Zaafria.

events.title: The guns pull out
events.text: At eleven 'part of the 17th Field Artillery left positions', taking some of K Company's 1st Platoon with it, and Lt. Harry Hoffman orders his infantry back. The battalion moves back by batteries toward an area south-west of the village. Drake reports all the artillery gone at one; Hoffman writes that the 17th left at three. Both may be right for different batteries. The replay shows one battery leaving at eleven, one at one and one at three; that split is a reconstruction.

events.title: The southern pincer
events.text: At noon the 21st Panzer Division arrives from the south. Kampfgruppe Schuette's advance guard, about thirty vehicles, enters the gap between Garet Hadid and Ksaïra, where Company C, 16th Armored Engineers covers a minefield, and fights there all afternoon. Kampfgruppe Stenkhoff, two tank battalions, has swung wide to Bir el Hafey. McQuillin moves his guns and command post out under dive-bomber attack; at 12:08 he signals 'Enemy right on top of us.' At one the 168th's headquarters starts for Garet Hadid.

events.title: Caught on the road
events.text: 'The 17th Field Artillery left their positions at 1500 hours.' Moving back by batteries, the battalion is dive-bombed again and again and, in Howe's words, 'destroyed as a fighting unit'; a 1st Armored officer writes of German tanks 'moving up from the south'. All its 155 mm howitzers are lost. Where and when each battery was hit is not recorded, and the bomb strikes on the map are placed by inference. Some of its men reached Drake on Garet Hadid. Cpl James E. Vause of the 17th Field Artillery was among those reported captured on 14 February; his record names the regiment, not his battalion or battery.

events.title: The pincers meet
events.text: At 3:30 Ziegler judges his first mission done. About four a company of Hudel's battalion enters Sidi Bou Zid and finds it empty. At 5:05 Stenkhoff, coming up the road from Bir el Hafey since 1:45, meets the 10th Panzer west of the village. Combat Command A has lost 44 tanks, all but two of its tank destroyers, nine of the 91st's guns and all the 155s. It rallies at dusk near Djebel Hamra.

events.title: Night on the hills
events.text: At seven the 3rd Battalion, 168th Infantry pulls back into the Ksaïra hills. Drake holds Garet Hadid with about 950 men, some 300 of them unarmed men from the tanks, reconnaissance units, tank destroyers and artillery. Waters's force is still on Lessouda. All three are cut off.

events.title: The counterattack
events.text: Combat Command C under Col. Robert Stack, with Lt. Col. James Alger's 2nd Battalion, 1st Armored Regiment, reaches its assembly area north-east of Djebel Hamra by 9:45 and attacks toward Sidi Bou Zid at 12:40. Dive bombers hit it at 1:40, about 2:40 and 4:30.

events.title: Still pretty busy
events.text: From about four the tanks are fighting near Sidi Salem and the village. Just after 4:45 comes Alger's last message: 'Still pretty busy. Situation in hand.' The armored infantry is clear by 5:40 and withdrawal is ordered at six. Of 52 tanks that went in, 46 are lost; Howe says only four came out. The 2nd Battalion reports 15 officers and 298 men missing, Alger among them. The Germans claim 39 tanks.

events.title: Out of Lessouda
events.text: About 10:30 the infantry on Lessouda breaks out across the plain. About a third of its 900 men get out: 231 reach Djebel Hamra before dawn and others reach Kern's Crossroads at five. Waters is captured on the 16th.

events.title: The decision is yours
events.text: All day on the 16th Ksaïra and Garet Hadid are under attack. At 2:30 Maj. Gen. Orlando Ward, commanding the 1st Armored Division, radios Drake: 'We can do no more for you. The decision is yours.' Late in the afternoon a withdrawal message is dropped on Ksaïra, about five by Drake's account and 4:30 by Line's.

events.title: Off the hills
events.text: The Garet Hadid column moves off between 9:50 and ten. The 3rd Battalion follows from Ksaïra about 11:40, once the code word comes through. Both march for Djebel Hamra, 22 to 26 miles by Drake's reckoning, under a moon Hoffman calls full, breaking through cloud.

events.title: Caught on the plain
events.text: About seven both columns are caught in the open by German motorised troops and tanks. Drake's group fights for about three and a half hours; Lt. William Rogers of the 91st and twelve volunteers are killed holding a knoll. Howe counts about 800 prisoners in the first group and 600, Drake among them, in the second; Van Vliet is taken too. The accounts put the place a few miles short of Djebel Hamra, but a grid reference in Line's report puts it about 6 km south-west of Sidi Bou Zid, which is where the map shows it. Which German units made the capture is not recorded here; the map's are a guess.

events.title: After
events.text: The 14th and 15th cost the 1st Armored Division 98 tanks, 57 half-tracks and 29 guns, and the 168th Infantry lost about 2,200 men of its 2nd and 3rd Battalions. The 21st Panzer Division claimed 2,546 Allied prisoners for 14–17 February: a German count of men taken, not of the dead. That day the 21st Panzer takes Sbeïtla and the 1st Armored falls back through Kasserine. Drake's men are marched back toward Lessouda, then trucked to Sfax and sent on by Tunis to Italy and the camps in Germany and Poland.

losses: 14 Feb, Combat Command A (Howe's final count): 6 killed, 22 wounded, 134 missing (Blumenson: 32 wounded); 44 tanks, all but two tank destroyers, nine of the 91st's 105s and all the 155s of the 17th FA; Blumenson adds 59 half-tracks and 26 guns. The first estimate on the 16th was 62 officers and 1,536 men killed, wounded or missing. 15 Feb, Combat Command C: 46 of 52 tanks; 15 officers and 298 men of the 2nd Battalion, 1st Armored Regiment missing. 168th Infantry: about 2,200 men of its 2nd and 3rd Battalions; some 1,400 taken on 17 Feb (Anderson; Howe counts about 800 and 600).
No German count found. The US estimate for 15 Feb alone was 13 Mark IVs, five 88 mm and ten other guns, and about 50 killed.
outcome.note: German claims of Allied losses: the 10th Panzer, 71 prisoners and 40 tanks on 14 Feb; the 21st Panzer, 2,546 prisoners, 103 tanks, 280 vehicles and 18 field guns for 14–17 Feb. Some accounts print the 2,546 as Americans killed; it is a German claim of prisoners taken. How many howitzers the 17th FA lost is uncertain: Atkinson says eighteen, a 2024 newspaper account twelve.

sources: George F. Howe, Northwest Africa: Seizing the Initiative in the West (US Army Center of Military History, 1957), chapters XXI and XXII and Map 11: the plan of Frühlingswind, the kampfgruppen and their axes, the clock times, the 17th FA's position and destruction (citing Lt. Col. Henry P. Ward to Col. Charles E. Hart, 16 Feb 1943, in the 17th FA regimental history), Combat Command C, the prisoners and the losses.

US Army Center of Military History, Kasserine Pass Battles: Readings, Vol. I, Part 1 (staff ride volume): the 1st Armored Division's report of operations; Hudel and Robinett, 'The Tank Battle at Sidi Bou Zid'; the 168th Infantry reports of Maj. Robert Moore, 1st Lt. Harry Hoffman (Co K), Lt. Col. Gerald Line and Col. Thomas Drake; the Lessouda Force history.
Martin Blumenson, 'Kasserine Pass, 30 January–22 February 1943', in America's First Battles (1986): the losses.
Rick Atkinson, An Army at Dawn (2002), chapter 9; Charles R. Anderson, Tunisia (CMH, 1993).
NARA, WWII Prisoners of War Data File (RG 389): Cpl James E. Vause, 17th Field Artillery Regiment, reported captured 14 February 1943.

GLO-30 sampled at 100 m over a 36 km square; it is a surface model, so the modern town of Sidi Bouzid and its irrigated farms show. Places from OpenStreetMap and the 1943 grid references; the roads are drawn straight between them, not traced.
Clock: the times as recorded, read as a GMT+1 clock, which fits 'light not yet sufficient' at 6:30; sunrise 7:10 and sunset 18:02 are computed for 14 February on that assumption.

What is reconstructed: every unit strength except the tank counts Howe and the reports give (German tank counts split Howe's divisional totals across the kampfgruppen); the three batteries of four howitzers each, their places along the road, which left when, and where each was caught; the times and places of the Stukas over the 17th FA; the routes between recorded places; how tank losses fell between companies; the German units at the capture on 17 February; and the hours of the fighting on 16 February.
